items.title: Howie Shear interviewed by Monk Rowe, Dunkirk, New York, October 11, 2014
items.q: it’s hard to think of a player, a guy like Joe Lovano, they all do other things that come along

ctx.x: I do get that question a lot. But I always say yet but you should be able to teach, you should be able to play, you should be able to compose, you should be able to orchestrate, you should be able to do almost anything you can in music in order to survive and so you won’t have to do anything else. If you just want to be a jazz player and nothing else it’s very difficult. Very, very difficult. There’s a couple of cities only to choose from. And there’s Europe of course, and there’s Asia, particularly Japan, and…
If you look at some of the — it’s hard to think of a player, a guy like Joe Lovano, they all do other things that come along.

Oh absolutely. Yeah, yeah, yeah. I think the greatest thing I ever did was learn how to play jazz. Two Augusts ago I was in Paris for two weeks. And when they hear you play, wherever it might be — this particular place was Paris — you just make friends immediately because it’s a language. And you might not speak French — but I happen to speak French so I got along great speaking French — but if I didn’t it wouldn’t matter because I speak jazz and all these jazz people who come out speak jazz, or they want to…
